kind: hand-written: four forecast records, the expected verdict of the validator on each, invented outcomes, invented file layouts, assumptions and the inputs of the learner task. Nothing in this file is measured in the repository; the observed data are in observed-input.json.
random_seed_note: No random number is drawn: every result is an exact count, or an exact rational computation rounded when it is written.

base_rate_windows.note: Analysis choice: a window lasts as long as the forecasts' horizon (92 days, from the pinned commit to the resolution time, rounded down to whole days). Windows are laid back to back, ending at the pinned commit, as many as fit after the first module commit. The alignment table moves the end back one day at a time, as long as the same number of windows still fits. The research cycle's hypothesis expected a broad base rate below 0.1; the table lists the alignments at which that holds.

records.status: worked example of a forecast record: an exercise in writing a forecast, not a commitment of the department and not a prediction it endorses
records.question: Will the Streeling course library hold more than 19 distinct Music modules at 2027-01-13T23:59:59Z?

value_at_writing.how: the counting rule below applied to state/streeling/courses at that commit

resolution_source.commit_rule: Fetched after resolution_time: the last commit of the first-parent chain of master (or of the default branch if master is renamed) whose committer date is at or before resolution_time, given by git rev-list -1 --first-parent --before=2027-01-13T23:59:59Z origin/master; then git ls-tree -r --name-only <commit> -- state/streeling/courses lists the files, each read at that commit.

resolution_rule.counts: Distinct module ids of the Music department, over .md files only. A file's module id is the module_id of its front matter or, when it has none, its file name without .md and without a language suffix such as .fr. A file belongs to Music when its front matter says department: music or, without one, when the nearest folder above it that is not a two-letter language folder is named music.
resolution_rule.unit: Each module id counts once, whatever the number of languages, copies or folders in which it appears.
resolution_rule.excluded: README.md and index.md pages, department records, files outside the library, and published copies such as the public site: only the source library counts.
resolution_rule.if_moved: If master, at the resolution commit, names another place as the library's source or as part of it (a README, a pointer file, or a commit message), apply the same rule there too, at that place's last commit at or before resolution_time, whether or not state/streeling/courses still exists; a module id found in several places counts once over all of them.
resolution_rule.void_if: No library can be found by these rules; commit 4b03838 is not an ancestor of the resolution commit; the record has no timestamp (see written_at_evidence) by resolution_time; or the rule's Music count differs from 19 at any first-parent commit of master after 4b03838 whose committer date precedes that timestamp. A void forecast is reported as void, never scored as 0.

records.reference_class: Streeling departments holding at least one English module at the start of a 92-day window, over the two back-to-back 92-day windows that end at commit 4b03838 (36 department-windows). Event: the department's module count at the end of the window exceeds its count at the start.

base_rate.command: git log --topo-order --reverse --no-renames --name-status --format='%H %ct' 4b03838800dcd4894f1e026461979bff1d985ca8 -- state/streeling/courses   (replay the added and deleted <department>/en/<name>.md paths, README.md excluded, and compare each department's count at the two window boundaries)

records.adjustment: Music is one of the two departments whose count rose in the latest window (6 to 19), and its newest module is dated on the day of the pinned commit. The Music-only class gives 1 rise in 2 windows, whose exact interval is too wide to set a number, so 0.7 is the author's judgment, written down before the outcome.

falsifier.statement: The count at the resolution commit is 19 or fewer: 0.7 then scores worse than the base rate would have, and the departure from the base rate failed on this question.

records.author_influence_note: The author of this record writes no Music module and cannot merge into the resolution source. R20 judges the record's author, whoever writes it, and nobody else: the maintainers who would merge this record also decide which modules of every department are merged (commit 4b03838 is itself the squash merge of pull request #1196, MUS-022). The record cannot remove that influence, only disclose it.
records.written_at_evidence: None yet beyond the author's statement: the record sits in an uncommitted file. Its timestamp will be the mergedAt time that GitHub records for the first GuitarAlchemist/Demerzel pull request that merges the record's final text into master (gh pr view <number> --json mergedAt), or a timestamping service's record of the file's hash, whichever is earlier. Not used: the pull request's createdAt, which dates the request and not its final text; push times, which GitHub's events API lists for 30 days only; and commit dates, which the committer's machine sets.

forecast.meaning: a central 80% interval by its stated level, which sets alpha = 0.2 in the interval score: lower is the author's 0.1 quantile, and upper is at or above the author's 0.9 quantile, since author_beliefs gives six chances in seven or more of 25 or fewer after a rise. With 0.3 on 19 itself (author_beliefs), the author's own probability that [19, 25] covers is at least 0.9, not 0.8.

author_beliefs.note: From the adjustment below: 1 - 0.7 on 19 itself, and six chances in seven or more of 25 or fewer modules if the count rises.

reference_forecast.meaning: persistence: in 34 of the 36 department-windows the count did not change, so both quantiles of the reference class are 'no change'

records.adjustment: Same reason as music-rise-2027-01-13, whose 0.7 leaves 0.3 on 19, so the 0.1 quantile stays at 19; if the count rises, the author puts 25 or fewer modules at six chances in seven or more, so the 0.9 quantile is at most 25, which is taken as the upper end.

falsifier.statement: The count at the resolution commit is 19 or fewer: the interval then scores worse than the persistence interval [19, 19].

expected_validation.note: Known answer, written before the first run: the rules each record must fail. An empty list means the record passes.

validator_controls.note: Copies of a worked record with one field changed, and the rules each copy must fail. The last probability control changes the forecast to its reference and must pass.

invented_outcomes.note: INVENTED outcomes, for illustration only. Nobody knows the real outcome before the resolution time; these values are neither observed nor forecast.

verbal_probability.note: Assumption for exercise 1: two readers turn the word 'likely' into two different numbers.

coverage_scale.note: Scale for one sentence of the lesson: how often ten intervals, each covering with probability 0.9 (the least coverage of the worked interval under its author's beliefs), cover seven times or fewer.

hypothetical_layouts.note: INVENTED file lists in the format of observed-input.json (path, front-matter module_id or '-', front-matter department or '-'), used to test the counting rule on situations a scorer may meet. Not observed.
